results.title: All 2026 targets achieved, excellence in execution, focus on value creation
highlights:
# All 2026 targets achieved, excellence in execution, focus on value creation 

 Tue, 10/20/2026 - 12:00 

- Revenue +7.2% like-for-like, adjusted EBITDA margin at 42%
- Levered Free Cash Flow positive for the first time since IPO
- FY2027 targets: accelerating value-creating growth

Octave Klaba, Chairman and CEO of OVHcloud, said:

> “Twelve months after my return, we have delivered on all of the targets we announced. Fourth-quarter revenue grew 10.5% on a like-for-like basis, and monthly revenue surpassed the €100 million milestone by the end of the fiscal year.
> 
> FY 2026 was a year of discipline. We managed our inventory and capex very closely while keeping operating costs under control. Customer acquisition and sales volumes were very strong across domain names, VPS and Bare Metal. Public Cloud revenue grew 20% in the fourth quarter. In response to rising RAM and storage prices, we made measured adjustments to our pricing. Our new sales organization, put in place during the year, will deliver its full impact from 2027.
> 
> We have redefined our AI strategy, and in 2027 we are moving into the deployment phase. In AI, our customers do not all have the same needs: our solutions serve several customer profiles, which limits the risk on our investments. We will continue to become more efficient. Simplifying the customer experience and regionalizing our Public Cloud offerings should allow us to accelerate our growth even further. The Group has now returned to its fundamentals and is ready to shift into a higher gear.”

...

Assets secured for FY27 In response to rising component prices, the Group has secured the supply of components required to support its growth. Thanks to very precise management of our component inventory, we can adapt to customer demand within just a few days, which helps limit the cash tied up. Each investment also remains subject to strict financial discipline, with a focus on value creation.

With 250 MW of connected power capacity, of which 140 MW is in operation, the Group has headroom for growth without needing to build new sites. The group is also exploring various scenarios for changing how its infrastructure is structured, with a view to potential capacity expansions and the ramp-up of its GPU business.

Inflation passed on in an immediate and measured manner The Group made targeted pricing adjustments based on a "mutualised pass-through" approach of the revaluation of the cost of components. The increase is applied to all recent and newly ordered servers. The aim is to keep supporting our customers’ growing demand in an inflationary environment.

...

In response to rising component costs, OVHcloud has chosen to anticipate part of its hardware investments. These include approximately €49.5 million of memory and disk components strictly intended for use in 2027. 

Excluding this anticipated capex, adjusted Capex represent 32.6% of revenue, below the target range of 33% to 35%, and can be broken down into: - hardware Capex (servers) of around €291 million, stable outside of anticipated capex - infrastructure and network Capex of around €53 million - stable product and software Capex of around €72 million

# Septembre 2026 sur le blog OVHcloud : notre récap

OVHcloud Team 13/10/2026 5 min de lecture

...

### AI Gigafactory : le business model introuvable ?

OVHcloud rejoindra-t-il un consortium AI Gigafactory ? Octave Klaba répond chiffres à l’appui. Le projet s’accorde sur bien des points avec le plan stratégique Step Ahead, mais trois éléments ne sont pas alignés : une logique uniquement nationale, l’obligation d’un site unique et une commande publique symbolique. Les 200 millions d’euros promis sur cinq ans ne couvrent qu’entre 10 % et 15 % du revenu nécessaire à l’équilibre, estimé entre 300 et 400 millions par an. La seule voie envisagée serait un nouveau consortium de grands utilisateurs de GPU. La décision reste ouverte, mais OVHcloud fournira une IA souveraine dans tous les cas. Suivez le raisonnement complet d’Octave Klaba.

...

### ADSL : la hausse au 1ᵉʳ septembre, la fibre en relais

Connecté en ADSL, VDSL ou SDSL ? Depuis le 1ᵉʳ septembre, le tarif des accès cuivre dégroupés OVHcloud augmente de 5 € HT par mois et par paire. Cette hausse découle de la fermeture programmée du réseau cuivre en France, attendue d’ici 2030, et ces coûts ne redescendront pas. La fibre est déjà raccordable dans près de 95 % des locaux. Pour basculer, la Fibre Pro (FTTH) et la Fibre dédiée (FTTO) sont proposées à -50 % pendant six mois, avec les frais d’accès offerts. Vérifiez les nouveaux tarifs et les deux parcours vers la fibre.

results.title: Letter to shareholders, employees and customers
highlights:
# Letter to shareholders, employees and customers

 Tue, 10/20/2026 - 12:00 

Dear shareholders, employees and customers, One year ago, in October 2025, I took back the helm of OVH Group with three objectives: to deliver on our performance commitments, to drive growth in Cloud and Artificial Intelligence, and to create sustainable value for our customers, employees and shareholders. To achieve this, the “Step Ahead” strategic plan relies on our famous “secret sauce”: executing today while preparing for tomorrow, collaborating with our customers and partners to anticipate their needs, and deploying short, progressive and disciplined investment cycles. Our strength? It’s the ecosystem we have brought together around OVH Group over the past 27 years. 3,200 employees who share the same values: trust, teamwork, passion, disruption and responsibility. Over one million customers and partners who rely on us 24/7. Financial partners who support our ambitions and have trusted us for years. One year later, we are ready to accelerate. Solid key industrial assets You can’t download a datacenter in one click. It takes years to build the critical infrastructure for Cloud and AI. Since our beginning, we have established the entire industrial value chain, from building datacenters to designing servers. This technological independence allows us to move faster and better control our costs. We own the vast majority of our datacenters, and a significant portion of their electrical capacity remains available. This strategic asset will support our next phase of growth. Our network is rarely mentioned, and that’s a good sign: it works! Over twenty years ago, we chose to invest in our own Internet network. Now global, it connects all our datacenters to each other and to the rest of the world. Over the past fifteen years, its annual cost has remained stable while its share of our revenue has steadily decreased. Any global Cloud and AI player needs a network of this scale. Ours has already largely paid for itself. Our supply chain and our two server production sites are also strategic assets. We can adapt to customer demand within a few days. This is the result of the reorganisation I initiated in FY2025. Since then, we have been managing our component inventory more closely to limit tied-up cash. Liquid cooling has become essential for GPUs. Drawing on twenty years of watercooling expertise, we are now adapting this technology at lower cost to new generations of GPUs, just as we do every quarter for our standard servers. An expanded software and commercial offering We are also a software business, with a well-known economic model: fixed costs and high margins. In five years, we have developed more than 80 Public Cloud products. Growth is accelerating, confirming increasingly rapid commercial adoption and the strategic relevance of creating additional products. We are now working on integrating these 80 products with one another and on regionalising our Public Cloud offering. The aim is to capture demand in Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific to further accelerate our growth. Bare Metal remains the essential building block of the Cloud: it attracts new customers and meets the needs of the largest ones. The price increase on our latest-generation servers generates additional cash flow that offsets the rising cost of RAM and disks, so that we can continue to fulfil our customers’ orders. At the same time, we have secured service continuity for our customers on VMware services through a multi-year contract, and we are working on the next steps. For customers with the highest sovereignty and security requirements, our third offering, “SNC Cloud Platform,” is available and is SecNumCloud certified. We have also started delivering “On-Prem Cloud Platform” to our customers’ datacenters. Altogether, our customers have access to the broadest portfolio of offerings among European players. We operate our three go-to-market models, Digital Starters, Digital Scalers and Corporate, in sixteen countries. The reorganisation of our teams carried out in FY2026 will take full effect in FY2027. In parallel, we will overhaul customer support: it will be better segmented and assisted by Artificial Intelligence to improve its quality and response times. Finally, we will clarify the value proposition of each of our brands: Kimsufi, SoYouStart, Gladia, OVH, OVHcloud and OVHai. A simplified organisation Our operating model rests on two pillars. ... On the other hand, small multidisciplinary teams, augmented by Artificial Intelligence, working on new projects.
